findings.criterion: Durable SQLite edge-journal retention must cover the exact declared recovery horizon.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires the effective edge-journal cleanup age to cover maximum_disconnect_seconds + maximum_replay_seconds + safety_margin_seconds. The seeded values make that boundary 237600 seconds (66 hours), but test_f2p_retention_policy_covers_recovery_horizon only proves that a 24-hour row is retained and a 72-hour row is eligible. An implementation that deletes at 48 or 60 hours can pass while deleting the only replay authority before the documented horizon expires.
findings.minimal_remediation: Grade the effective journal-age boundary against the computed required_horizon_seconds itself (for example with cases immediately below and above that boundary, or an equivalent behavioral assertion) while keeping the separate JetStream max-age checks.
findings.regression_risk: Premature cleanup inside the documented recovery horizon can make a disconnect/replay incident unrecoverable even though every verifier case passes.

findings.criterion: Restart consumer-progress validation must compare durable application state with observed external JetStream consumer state.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract explicitly makes the JetStream acknowledgement floor external evidence on restart. The negative verifier case writes jetstream_ack_floor directly into the same SQLite consumer_checkpoints row and calls consumer_health(); the report reconstruction also reads that persisted value. No verifier path observes a live JetStream durable consumer ack floor. A controller that never queries JetStream on restart, or that merely trusts/self-populates the SQLite floor, can satisfy the suite while missing the required split-brain/state-loss detection.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a behavioral restart/health case whose JetStream consumer state is obtained from a real NATS/JetStream consumer and differs from the durable effect/checkpoint ledger, then require the operator-visible health/reconciliation outcome to expose the mismatch.
findings.regression_risk: A stale or advanced server ack floor can be accepted as safe application progress, losing effects after restart.

findings.criterion: Archive membership, not replay-item completion state, must remain replay authority at execution/resume time; already-archived plan items are no-ops.
findings.why_it_matters: Planning-time tests prove that newly created plans contain missing identities, and fencing tests can leave a replay item in PUBLISHED state, but no test resumes that plan while the archive identity is still absent. Conversely, no execution test presents a plan item that became archived after planning and verifies that it is skipped. A wrong executor can trust replay_plan_items.state as completion authority or republish an identity already present in the archive and still pass all 40 tests.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add execution/resume behavior that (a) reprocesses a PUBLISHED/completed replay item when archive membership is still missing and (b) treats an item that became archived after planning as an execution-time no-op, using stable archive identity as the decision boundary.
findings.regression_risk: Recovery can either strand a real archive gap or replay an already archived event, violating the exactly-once recovery contract.

findings.criterion: JetStream delivery acknowledgement must occur only after durable effect commit and application-checkpoint advancement.
findings.why_it_matters: The commit-failure test asserts only that SQLite effect/ack checkpoints do not advance when commit_effect raises. It does not assert that the delivery itself was not acknowledged. A processor can acknowledge JetStream before attempting the effect commit, then leave the SQLite checkpoints unchanged when commit fails, and still satisfy the test while permanently discarding the delivery.
findings.minimal_remediation: In the effect-commit failure path, behaviorally assert that the delivery is not acknowledged (and remains redeliverable), in addition to asserting that application progress did not advance.
findings.regression_risk: Acknowledging before durable effect completion creates an unrecoverable lost-effect window.

findings.criterion: Origin-generation reset detection and end-to-end origin metadata/header agreement must be fully graded.
findings.why_it_matters: The generation-regression fixture lowers sequence while also changing the stream fingerprint, so it does not prove that a lower sequence under an otherwise matching fingerprint is independently held as the contract requires. The test named generation_header_mismatch_is_rejected never supplies mismatched JetStream headers; it only references an unapproved generation in the EventEnvelope. The real replay readback checks event_id and physical Nats-Msg-Id but not region, origin_generation, origin_sequence, payload_sha256, or their origin headers. Implementations can ignore physical origin-header agreement or key reset handling only on fingerprint changes and still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a lower-sequence observation with the current fingerprint that must enter the pending/held path, and add an external/message-boundary case that validates the documented origin fields/header agreement rather than only Nats-Msg-Id.
findings.regression_risk: Events from a recreated/ambiguous origin can be merged into the wrong generation or lose authoritative origin metadata while appearing healthy.

findings.criterion: Every named reconciliation metadata dimension must have negative behavioral coverage.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires validation of origin metadata for every matching identity and separately names payload checksum mismatches. The dedicated negative test mutates source_domain and payload_sha256, but does not force a same-event origin_sequence mismatch or a wrong source_stream. The final report oracle calculates those dimensions only on the unchanged seeded rows, so a reconciliation implementation that ignores source_stream and same-ID origin_sequence mismatches can still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add independent negative mutations for the remaining contractual match metadata (at least source_stream and same-event origin_sequence) and require divergence/count/finding behavior without prescribing implementation structure.
findings.regression_risk: A physically misattributed or resequenced archive record can be accepted as a valid match, corrupting recovery truth.

findings.criterion: Stable reconciliation count semantics must be discoverable from the solver-visible contract.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract lists origin metadata mismatches and payload checksum mismatches as separate reconciliation outputs, while the stable report exposes metadata_mismatch_count without defining whether checksum failures are folded into it. The verifier requires one source-domain mismatch plus one checksum mismatch to produce metadata_mismatch_count == 2. It also defines duplicate_count as the sum of archive_index.duplicate_observation_count, a meaning not stated by the stable report contract. A semantically reasonable implementation can report checksum findings separately or count duplicate identities rather than duplicate observations and fail the verifier.
findings.minimal_remediation: Define the operator-facing aggregation semantics for metadata_mismatch_count and duplicate_count in the delegated contract, or relax/reshape the verifier so it grades only semantics the contract actually specifies.
findings.regression_risk: Legitimate implementations can fail solely because of undocumented report aggregation vocabulary, while operators receive an unstable public schema.

findings.criterion: Poison-event grading must enforce observable quarantine/no-progress semantics rather than an undocumented internal effect-row representation.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires poison input to be recorded in the quarantine table and not counted as a completed business effect or completed application progress. The verifier additionally requires engine.store.effect(...) to return a processing_effects row whose exact EffectStatus is QUARANTINED. The solver-visible contract never requires a poison item to exist in processing_effects at all. A valid design that records only poison_events, emits no business dispatch, and leaves application progress unchanged will fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Grade the documented quarantine record, absence of committed/duplicated business effect, and unchanged completed progress. Keep the exact processing_effects QUARANTINED representation only if it is intentionally promoted into the solver-visible contract.
findings.regression_risk: The verifier unnecessarily freezes a private persistence representation and rejects otherwise correct recovery behavior.

findings.criterion: Consumer-gap grading must not require undocumented private diagnostic keys.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires the controller to report a restart gap, and the stable health interface explicitly makes details optional without defining their internal keys. test_f2p_restart_detects_ack_floor_effect_ledger_gap directly calls the private engine consumer_health() detail structure and requires a field named state_gap with value 50. A compliant implementation can report consumers_ok=false and expose the mismatch under a different optional diagnostic shape yet fail this assertion.
findings.minimal_remediation: Assert the documented operator-visible unhealthy/gap behavior and durable values without requiring state_gap, or document state_gap as a stable public detail field if that exact key is truly required.
findings.regression_risk: A private return-value vocabulary becomes an accidental hidden public contract.

findings.criterion: Cleanup-safe sequence must be graded as the documented minimum, not merely as an upper bound below each safety watermark.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract defines cleanup_safe_sequence as the minimum of three authorities. The F2P tests assert safe_sequence <= each relevant bound, while P2P cases only require a few very old low-sequence rows to become eligible. A substantially over-conservative constant safe sequence (for example one just above the seeded low P2P rows) can satisfy all retention tests without computing the contractual minimum, leaving large amounts of legitimately cleanable journal state permanently retained.
findings.minimal_remediation: Use scenarios in which each authority is the unique minimum and assert the resulting cleanup-safe sequence equals that minimum, while retaining the age/hold protections.
findings.regression_risk: The repaired controller can pass while failing the documented retention algorithm and accumulating unbounded durable journal state.

findings.criterion: Stable generated_at fields must have a solver-visible type/format/time-zone contract if the verifier enforces one.
findings.why_it_matters: The delegated contract says only that each stable report includes a generated_at timestamp. The verifier requires generated_at to be a non-empty string parseable by datetime.fromisoformat and to contain timezone information. Those representation requirements are not discoverable from the stable report contract; an epoch timestamp or another legitimate timestamp encoding can satisfy the written contract and fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Document the timestamp representation (for example an offset-aware ISO-8601/RFC3339 string) if that format is required, or loosen the verifier to accept the timestamp forms permitted by the contract.
findings.regression_risk: A valid report can be rejected for an undocumented serialization choice in a field explicitly declared stable.

findings.criterion: Stable health subsystem booleans must have discoverable semantic predicates when the verifier reconstructs and compares them exactly.
findings.why_it_matters: The stable interface names topology_ok, generations_ok, publication_ok, archive_ok, consumers_ok, retention_ok and recovery_ok and defines only healthy as their conjunction. The verifier imposes specific hidden predicates, including recovery_ok iff there are no active plans, publication_ok iff no PUBLISHING/RETRY/HELD rows exist, consumers_ok iff effect==ack==persisted JetStream floor, and retention_ok from stream max-age checks. Those exact subsystem definitions are not stated as stable report semantics. A report can truthfully describe the durable state under a reasonable interpretation and still fail exact field comparisons.
findings.minimal_remediation: Either document the semantic predicate for every stable subsystem boolean at the invariant level, including how journal retention participates in retention_ok, or grade only relations/outcomes the current contract defines.
findings.regression_risk: The verifier silently turns intuitive field names into hidden status vocabulary and can reject behaviorally correct implementations.
